name: Elam
overview: The biblical topic of Elam encompasses both a geographical region southeast of Babylon and several individuals connected to Israel's history. Scripture identifies Elam as a kingdom led by Chedorlaomer during the time of Abraham, highlighting its ancient political significance (Genesis 14:1, 9). Additionally, Elam refers to a group of Jewish captives, whose descendants numbering twelve hundred fifty-four, returned from Babylonian exile, demonstrating God's faithfulness in restoring His people (Ezra 2:7, 31; Nehemiah 7:12). The presence of Levites and leaders named Elam in the post-exilic community further underscores their role in worship and governance as part of Israel's covenantal restoration (Ezra 8:7).
